richSourceDetails: Original IM 2021 G5 U05:L08 Round Decimals: students label NUMBER-LINE ticks, estimate a point between marked decimals, and round printed decimal numbers to nearest whole, tenth and hundredth. Rounding requires comparing distances on a correctly scaled line, not simply changing a digit mechanically without understanding the threshold.

Warm-up Estimation Exploration Number Line: the publisher shows an unlabeled point and asks low/about-right/high estimates. Original line figure not independently reproduced, so its exact point is teacher-reviewed and not automatically assigned a fabricated coordinate.

Activity 1 Name that Number: printed Jada point labeled15.53 on 11 evenly spaced ticks from15 to16 (tenths). Source places point between the sixth and seventh tick marks; determine whether 15.53 lies in the correct 15.5–15.6 interval and assess the original plotted point position with the actual visual, rather than assume a source image match from alt text alone. Other original lines are3–4 by tenths,5.6–5.7 by hundredths and1.7–1.8 by hundredths, with points between specific marks. These image-dependent estimate answers are TEACHER_REVIEW_REQUIRED.

Activity 2 Which Number Is Closest?: source6.273 rounds nearest whole6, tenth6.3, hundredth6.27. Original4.158 rounds whole4, tenth4.2, hundredth4.16. Children can use source number lines to justify nearest bounds and the place immediately right of rounding digit.

Activity 3 Round the Numbers optional: printed original table numbers34.482,99.909,5.555,19.509. Nearest whole/tenth/hundredth respectively:34/34.5/34.48;100/99.9/99.91;6/5.6/5.56;20/19.5/19.51. Apply Grade5 conventional five-rounds-up half-way policy and handle carrying to a new whole at99.909 and19.509.
